policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV renders a transitive causative, "when I shall bring back the captivity of Judah and Jerusalem", which is the hiphil qere ashiv (I will cause to return) with the captivity as its object. The ketiv ashuv is qal "I shall return", which the ASV wording does not carry. The lone note is classed alternative_rendering ("Or, return to"), so it bears only on English wording and does not decide the reading; the main-text wording does.
